key_insight: PyraTok introduces a pyramidal tokenizer that produces discrete video tokens at multiple spatiotemporal scales and aligns them with language, improving cross-modal correspondence and zero‑shot transfer compared to single‑scale codebooks.
problem_solved: Existing discrete video tokenizers use a single-scale codebook with limited vocabulary and weak language supervision, causing poor semantic alignment between video tokens and text and limiting zero‑shot transfer and generation quality.
method: Build on a pretrained video VAE and replace its single-scale codebook with a pyramidal set of discrete latents that capture multiple spatiotemporal resolutions.

Apply language supervision to the multi-scale codebooks so tokens become semantically aligned to text (e.g., contrastive or classifier-based alignment between token-level features and text embeddings).
Train and integrate the pyramidal tokenizer so downstream models (generation and understanding) can attend to coarse-to-fine semantic tokens for better cross-modal transfer and sample fidelity.
impact: Provides a practical way to obtain semantically structured, multi-resolution video tokens that improve text-video alignment, boosting zero-shot performance and quality for both video understanding and text-to-video generation. This enables more robust, scalable multimodal systems without retraining entire generative models from scratch.
visual_elements: Pyramidal diagram showing multiple spatiotemporal scales (coarse → fine) with arrows to discrete codebooks at each level.
Flowchart: pretrained video VAE → PyraTok multi-scale tokenizer → language alignment (text embeddings) → downstream tasks (generation/understanding).

paper_title: PyraTok: Language-Aligned Pyramidal Tokenizer for Video Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Onkar Susladkar, Tushar Prakash, Adheesh Juvekar, Kiet A. Nguyen, Dong-Hwan Jang
